sections.title: What you already know
sections.content: You know *dijo que* and reported speech from B1 Unit 13: after *dijo que* the present becomes the imperfect (*continúan* becomes *continuaban*), the perfect becomes the pluperfect (*ha dejado* becomes *había dejado*) and the future becomes the conditional (*firmaremos* becomes *firmarían*). When you write about a conflict, it keeps the source clear: it is the commission or the delegate who says it, not you.

sections.title: From direct words to reported speech
rows: Una delegada dijo que las conversaciones continuaban.
Dijo que habían escuchado a muchas víctimas.

items.spanish: Una delegada dijo que las conversaciones continuaban.
items.english: A delegate said that the talks were continuing.

items.spanish: La Comisión de la Verdad dijo en su informe de 2022 que el conflicto había dejado cientos de miles de muertos.
items.english: In its 2022 report, the Truth Commission said that the conflict had left hundreds of thousands dead.

items.spanish: El gobierno dijo que firmaría un nuevo acuerdo.
items.english: The government said it would sign a new agreement.

items.spanish: Según la ONU, las FARC entregaron casi nueve mil armas.
items.english: According to the UN, the FARC handed over almost nine thousand weapons.

sections.content: Use *dijo que* when the verb in the reported part moves back in time. *Según* (B1 Unit 13) gives the source without moving the tense: *Según la ONU, entregaron casi nueve mil armas*. Either way, say who is speaking.
